newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU to open talks on customs agreement with Norway.
newsitem.headline: EU to open talks on customs agreement with Norway.

text.p: The Internal Market Council on Friday authorised the European Commission to open talks with Norway on a customs agreement, the Irish Presidency said in a statement.

The accord would be a response to the situation created when Norway's voters decided their country should not enter the European Union at the same time as neighbours Sweden and Finland, with whom it currently holds such an agreement.

The existing agreements between Sweden and Norway and between Finland and Norway, under which Norwegian officials carry out customs tasks in remote border areas on behalf of the two countries, are not compatible with Community law.
Under the agreement to be negotiated, Norwegian officials would be able to carry out the customs duties, not only on behalf of Sweden and Finland, but on behalf of the EU as a whole.

Member states had harboured reservations about setting a precedent by allowing a non-member to carry out customs checks on behalf of the EU, but they came round to agree that Oslo was a special case, diplomats said.
